content:
sarah: alert from audit pipeline: detected an RBAC change on KMS key 'prod-app-key' granting iam.serviceAccountUser to svc-data-mover@proj.rolling.

sarah: this looks automated? change happened 03:42 UTC, origin=ci-cd-pipeline.

audit-bot: ADDED binding: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter -> serviceAccount:svc-data-mover@proj.rolling (actor: pipeline-runner@infra-ci)

nate: copying logs into thread, pulling recent IAM audit entries now.

leo: 3 quick asks: 1) is there active decrypt traffic from that SA? 2) can we revoke the binding fast? 3) do we rotate key?

priya: @nate check flow logs -> looks like 03:45..03:50 had ~120 decrypt calls from that SA to prod-app-key. not sure if successful.

nate: decrypts succeeded (200). stack traces show invoked by data-mover job that pulls and decrypts user embeddings for scrape job.

maya: tagging this as P1 until we confirm scope. I'll open a war-room on Zoom.

devsec: quick containment plan: 1) revoke new binding 2) disable SA 3) rotate key primary (create new version) 4) re-encrypt minimal set + rollback pipeline trigger.

leo: I can revoke binding now. running: `gcloud kms keys remove-iam-policy-binding prod-app-key --member='serviceAccount:svc-data-mover@proj.rolling' --role='roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter' --location=global --keyring=prod`

sarah: doing it with you, Nate watching logs.

deploy-bot: IAM binding removal started by leo at 03:55 UTC.

nate: removal completed, see audit: REMOVED binding at 03:56 UTC. but decrypt calls continued until 03:58 (maybe cached tokens).

priya: disabling the SA now: `gcloud iam service-accounts disable svc-data-mover@proj.rolling`

maya: good. DevSec, can we assume no lateral movement? what else to check?

devsec: check recent access to secrets, storage, and compute. also check createKeyVersion or import events.

nate: quick grep of cloud audit logs: no createKeyVersion, no key import. storage access spike: job wrote to gs://tmp-embeds for a minute. listing objects and author metadata.

leo: starting key rotation: create new key version v2 and set as primary. `gcloud kms keys versions create --key prod-app-key --location global --keyring prod`

deploy-bot: new key version v2 created at 04:10 UTC by leo.

priya: re-encrypt plan: re-encrypt only objects created in window 03:42-03:58. I will run a targeted rewrap job that fetches objects modified in that window and re-encrypts with v2.

nate: capturing timeline & evidence for postmortem. saving logs + list of objects, linking to S3 export: https://internal-storage/redwood/incidents/1719004321/export.tar.gz

maya: assigning owners: containment owner=leo, evidence= n ate, remediation=priya, comms=maya. Handoff to daytime oncall at 12:00 UTC.

devsec: temp mitigation completed. items remaining: run key compromise analysis, review CI pipeline that added binding, add guardrails to pipeline (prevent iam modifications without review), add monitoring alert for KMS binding changes.

leo: notes for handoff: revoked binding, disabled SA, rotated key to v2, re-encrypt job queued (IDs: rewrap-171900-1). no evidence of exfil beyond temp gs objects.

priya: re-encrypt finished at 05:02 UTC. 98 objects rewrapped. checksums match after re-encrypt.

nate: wrote Slack thread summary + timeline and uploaded to incident tracker ticket INC-2026-1723. adding playbook links: https://wiki/internal/sec/kms-incident-playbook

maya: leaving handoff notes -> day shift, please validate no consumer errors (500s) from decrypt failures, and confirm pipeline fix rolled.

devsec: recommended post-incident actions (short list): 1) rotate any keys accessed by that SA (done) 2) audit CI perms and remove iam admin from non-human runners 3) enforce Terraform-only IAM changes or require approvals 4) enable binding-change alert in observability.

leo: ack. I'm adding a runbook PR now to harden pipeline: https://git.internal/infra/ci-policies/pull/342

maya: handing off to daytime oncall @simon @anna — full notes in ticket. I will join overlap call at 12:05 UTC.

sarah: thanks team. will add this to postmortem queue and tag compliance for any audit reporting.

nate: final logs exported to secure bucket. locking export TTL to 90 days.

maya: closing war-room. leaving thread open for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
